lesson.menu_desc: Our last lesson: a farewell night out, your English then and now, and the answer from lesson 1 told again with everything you have learned -- 13 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 13 -- The Night Out
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Eglis Roberto | Lesson 13 -- The Night Out

listenings.text: Last Friday was my friend Harry's farewell. He is moving to Portugal next month, so twelve of us went out to say goodbye. We started at the bar at the marina, where Harry has been a regular for twenty years. Everybody there knows his name. I bought the first round, and his wife made a toast. Then something funny happened. I ran into a man I used to sail with in the eighties. I had not seen him for thirty years! We sat in a corner and caught up for an hour. He told me he had lost his boat in a storm, and that he was sailing again at seventy. We stayed out late, much later than we had planned. When I was young, I used to stay out until sunrise. Not anymore. At two in the morning, I called it a night. We have promised to keep in touch, and this time I think we will.

I am sixty-four, and two years ago I started to learn Italian. At the beginning, I was so nervous that I did not open my mouth in class. Last month I went to Rome, and my teacher's friends invited me for a night out. I almost said no. I thought, they will speak too fast, and I will just sit there and smile. But I went. The first hour was hard. I kept asking, sorry, could you say that again? Then a man asked me where I had learned Italian, and I told him the whole story. We talked about films, about food, about our children. Nobody corrected me, and nobody cared about my mistakes. At midnight, somebody made a toast to the brave lady from Toronto. I did not call it a night until two. If somebody had told me this two years ago, I would not have believed it.
